draft.title: Causes of the Second World War
card: These built up over years and made war more likely. They are the background to the war, not the event that started it.
This 1919 peace treaty ended the First World War. It punished Germany with lost land, limits on its army and payments for war damage. Many Germans felt angry and humiliated.
The economic crisis of the 1930s left millions of people without work. Many Germans turned to leaders who promised to fix their problems, and Hitler gained support.

These were the events close to the start of the war. Hitler expanded German territory in the late 1930s. Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France then declared war on Germany.
draft.remember: Long-term causes built tension over years. Short-term causes were the events just before war began.

a.q: Which of these is best described as a long-term cause of the Second World War?
opts: The harsh peace terms placed on Germany in 1919
Germany's invasion of Poland in September 1939
Britain and France declaring war on Germany
Hitler's moves to expand German territory in 1938
a.why: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919 and its effects built up for twenty years, so it is a long-term cause. The invasion of Poland happened right at the start of the war, so it is a short-term cause.
a.clue: Which one happened long before the war began?

b.q: Daniel says the Great Depression helped cause the Second World War. Which reason best supports his claim?
opts: Mass unemployment led many Germans to back Hitler
It forced Germany to invade Poland in 1939
It was the peace treaty that ended the First World War
It happened in the weeks before the war began
b.why: Widespread unemployment made many Germans willing to support leaders who promised change, and Hitler gained support. It was a long-term cause because it built over years. It did not force the invasion of Poland, which was a decision Hitler made later.
b.clue: Think about how hardship in the 1930s changed German politics.

a.best: The harsh peace terms placed on Germany in 1919

b.best: Mass unemployment led many Germans to back Hitler
